Hot Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade Gets Even Hotter With 2027 Mechanical and Visual Upgrades
56 photos
Photo: Honda
Japanese bike maker Honda has a product so successful and intense that it rarely needs to do anything to it to keep it relevant. Yet, as impressive as it is, the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade does need a refresh from time to time, and that's exactly what its maker announced this week at the EICMA show in Milan, Italy.
The last time Honda made some serious upgrades to the two-wheeler was a couple of years ago, but now, with all the deep changes announced this week, we'll need to reset the clock on that.
Although basically the same 1,000cc sports motorcycle as it's been over the past few years, the 2027 Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade throws in many new things, both internally and externally, so it's definitely worth a closer look.
As the base of tried and tested race bikes, the new Fireblade makes use of the same frame as before, but with modified rigidity balance and steering geometry, and accompanied by a lighter swingarm.
The suspension system stays the same Showa setup as before, but the forks and shock now tie into new and lighter 17-inch wheels, which are both equipped with Nissin braking hardware.
It's in the engine department that the most changes have been made. Even if they don't really alter the powerplant's performance levels, they are meant to make the Fireblade an even more unstoppable beast on the track.
The bike's liquid-cooled inline four-cylinder heart is good for 215 hp at 14,000 rpm and 114 Nm of torque at 10,500 rpm, but it now utilizes variable air funnels, throttle-by-wire, and revised cam timing, among other things.
On a hardware level, the 1,000cc engine got fitted with magnesium covers, aluminum bolts, and new crankcases – all of them selected as a means for the motorcycle to drop some weight – more specifically, 2.2 pounds (one kg) compared to the 2024 model year Fireblade.
To go with the few revisions to the bodywork, Honda opted to gift the bike with a brand-new aero package. It looks different from what it used to, but it does the same job as the previous setup – and Honda admitted as much.
Developed with assistance from the HRC WorldSBK team, the package swaps the previous winglet design for the fairing for a mid-section aero device. Apparently, the new solution delivers the same levels of downforce as before.
Honda installed a new LED headlight up front, redrew the front spoiler, remade the 4.4-gallon (16.6 liters) fuel tank in titanium, and raised the seat height a bit. Additionally, it also installed new lower cowl aerodynamic sidepods.
The Japanese do not specifically say when the world will get to meet the new Honda beast, but they did share that the 2027 model year will be offered both as the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP and CBR1000RR-R Fireblade HRC Works Edition. We're waiting for pricing to be revealed so that we can tell you that as well.
